opening_message:
Ticket 1: Alexandra Johnson (employee ID E003) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E003.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Alexandra Johnson (E003) is a full-time Analyst requesting admin on Source Code. Full-time employees max is write unless their role owns the system; Analyst does not own Source Code, so admin is not permitted. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security check: Alexandra Johnson (E003) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors max is read (write only with advanced training, never admin). Since admin is requested but not permitted, recommend granting read.
reason: Alexandra Johnson (E003) requested admin on Source Code. The two agent notes conflict on employment type: one says full-time Analyst (max write, since Analyst does not own Source Code), the other says contractor with basic security training (max read, never admin). Admin is above the maximum under both readings. Given the conflicting evidence, I grant the more restrictive permitted level (read), which is compliant with both possible employment classifications and never exceeds the request.
